messages.content: Predict the participant's actual entered report. Reply with exactly one integer: 1, 2 or 3, without explanation. The physical six-sided die has two faces each labelled 1, 2 and 3; each outcome has probability 1/3. The participant shakes a covered cup, privately observes the top face through a hole, and is instructed to enter that outcome immediately. The report is what determines earnings; the recorded report does not establish the physical result or truthfulness. Participants can practise the die before the experiment. This anonymous laboratory experiment has exactly three parts and a final questionnaire. Instructions for each later part are handed out only after the preceding part ends. At the end one whole part is randomly selected for payment for all participants; the three parts have separate earnings. There is EUR 2.50 for punctual arrival. Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 is a single individual report, without interaction. Entering 1 adds EUR 0, 2 adds EUR 3, and 3 adds EUR 6. Later estimation questions can earn an additional amount; their detailed instructions come later. The exact total and selected part are disclosed at the experiment end.

Current task: Part 1, its one round.
Participant information: age 21 years; recorded as female. These stable attributes were collected in the final questionnaire.
The participant knows their private die result, but the available record does not supply it.

Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. The current decision structure is: The randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first. The second sees that report and then rolls and reports. The third sees both earlier reports and then rolls and reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: The randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first. The second sees that report and then rolls and reports. The third sees both earlier reports and then rolls and reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: A randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first; that report is shown to both followers, who then roll and report simultaneously without seeing one another's current reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: All three roll and report simultaneously. No current peer report is visible before this choice.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: The randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first. The second sees that report and then rolls and reports. The third sees both earlier reports and then rolls and reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: The randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first. The second sees that report and then rolls and reports. The third sees both earlier reports and then rolls and reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: All three roll and report simultaneously. No current peer report is visible before this choice.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: A randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first; that report is shown to both followers, who then roll and report simultaneously without seeing one another's current reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: A randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first; that report is shown to both followers, who then roll and report simultaneously without seeing one another's current reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: A randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first; that report is shown to both followers, who then roll and report simultaneously without seeing one another's current reports.

Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: A randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first; that report is shown to both followers, who then roll and report simultaneously without seeing one another's current reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: A randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first; that report is shown to both followers, who then roll and report simultaneously without seeing one another's current reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: A randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first; that report is shown to both followers, who then roll and report simultaneously without seeing one another's current reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: A randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first; that report is shown to both followers, who then roll and report simultaneously without seeing one another's current reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: The randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first. The second sees that report and then rolls and reports. The third sees both earlier reports and then rolls and reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: All three roll and report simultaneously. No current peer report is visible before this choice.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: The randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first. The second sees that report and then rolls and reports. The third sees both earlier reports and then rolls and reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: The randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first. The second sees that report and then rolls and reports. The third sees both earlier reports and then rolls and reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: The randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first. The second sees that report and then rolls and reports. The third sees both earlier reports and then rolls and reports.

Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: A randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first; that report is shown to both followers, who then roll and report simultaneously without seeing one another's current reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: A randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first; that report is shown to both followers, who then roll and report simultaneously without seeing one another's current reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: A randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first; that report is shown to both followers, who then roll and report simultaneously without seeing one another's current reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: A randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first; that report is shown to both followers, who then roll and report simultaneously without seeing one another's current reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: All three roll and report simultaneously. No current peer report is visible before this choice.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: All three roll and report simultaneously. No current peer report is visible before this choice.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: A randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first; that report is shown to both followers, who then roll and report simultaneously without seeing one another's current reports.

Each part has an initial EUR 6 endowment paid with the selected part. Funds not spent here can finance future research. Participants sit in private cubicles; no communication is allowed, on pain of exclusion without compensation. Actual identities are not revealed. Part 1 involved an individual report with bonuses EUR 0/3/6 for reports 1/2/3, followed by estimates of how many other people in the room reported each number. Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. All three reports equal to 1 gives each EUR 3 extra; all equal to 2 gives each EUR 6; all equal to 3 gives each EUR 9; every other combination gives each EUR 0. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Part 3 has 30 rounds with the same two partners and the same fixed order as Part 2. Each round uses a new private roll and report. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed. The current decision structure is: A randomly assigned first mover rolls and reports first; that report is shown to both followers, who then roll and report simultaneously without seeing one another's current reports.

Those completed own answers are supplied below. In Part 2, random matching independent of Part 1 forms a group of three anonymous people. Each privately rolls and enters one number. After all reports, each sees all three reported numbers and the resulting bonus, never the others' actual private rolls. Three reports all 1/2/3 give each EUR 0.10/0.20/0.30 that round, respectively; otherwise each gets EUR 0. All 30 round bonuses are added to the single EUR 6 Part 3 endowment if this part is selected; no one round is selected instead. After each round all three reports and its bonus are revealed.
